RuntimeError: Triton Error [CUDA]: a
applicable_when: The kernel reads from a flat (7840,64) tensor and writes into a strided (10,64,28,28) output with column stride 480. The current 1D tiling (XBLOCK=128) maps flat indices directly to the strided output via x0 + 480*x1, causing non-coalesced scatter stores: consecutive threads write to addresses 480 floats apart, thrashing L1TEX and causing 21.8-cycle average stall per warp. This explains 78.74% idle scheduler cycles. The fix is to tile the 2D (row x col) space explicitly so that the 64-element column dimension (stride-1 in input, stride-1 in output x0 axis) is handled by the inner XBLOCK tile, making both loads AND stores coalesced within each warp. Prior attempts at @triton.autotune with 1D XBLOCK failed due to a Triton binary-load error (likely a constexpr naming collision in autotune configs); the new plan avoids this by using a clean 2D decomposition with separate XBLOCK and YBLOCK constexprs.
